title: Frequently Asked Questions
subtitle: Everything you need to know about ACIKY, our classes and Kundalini Yoga

cat1.title: About ACIKY
cat1.a1: ACIKY is the Cuban Alliance of Kundalini Yoga Instructors, an organization that brings together KRI-certified instructors in Cuba to organize, strengthen and expand the practice of Kundalini Yoga across the island.
cat1.q2: Does ACIKY have another official name?
cat1.a2: Yes. ACIKY is also the National Kundalini Yoga Teachers Association of Cuba (NKYTA), affiliated with IKYTA, the International Kundalini Yoga Teachers Association.
cat1.a3: It was officially established on June 26, 2025, after years of Cuban instructors independently organizing gatherings, retreats and classes. The Faro de Luz Festival, already running, was recognized as its flagship event.
cat1.a4: It's an ancient practice that combines physical postures (kriyas), breathing techniques (pranayama), meditation and mantras to awaken vital energy and elevate consciousness, reducing stress and promoting greater balance and purpose.
cat1.q5: Who taught this lineage of Kundalini Yoga?
cat1.a5: ACIKY teaches Kundalini Yoga as transmitted by Master Yogi Bhajan (1929–2004), who brought this tradition from East to West in 1969.
cat1.a6: To elevate and empower Kundalini Yoga teachers in Cuba, supporting their practice, strengthening yoga communities, and sharing the sacred science of Kundalini Yoga in every corner of the country.
cat1.q7: Does ACIKY have a single leader?
cat1.a7: No. Decisions are made collectively through a Steering Committee, without a single leadership figure.
cat1.q8: Which organizations does ACIKY collaborate with?
cat1.a8: Its alliances include Casa de Asia (official headquarters since 2019), the Office of the Historian of Havana, the Embassy of India in Cuba, IKYTA, 3HO, the Cuban Yoga Association, Om Meditación, Basanti Escuela, Dluzverde, Centro Árbol and Somos Imperfectos.
cat1.q9: In which Cuban provinces does ACIKY have a presence?
cat1.a9: ACIKY currently has a presence in 3 provinces (Havana, Matanzas and Cienfuegos) and is actively working to expand to all 15 provinces of the country through the Golden Routes project.

cat2.title: Classes and in-person practice
cat2.q1: How can I see the class schedule?
cat2.a1: The "Classes" section of the site publishes the updated weekly schedule.
cat2.a2: In-person classes and meditations take place at spaces like Casa Museo de Asia, among other practice locations ACIKY keeps adding across Cuba.
cat2.a3: Yes, ACIKY offers a free first class so new participants can try the practice with no commitment.
cat2.q4: What should I bring to class?
cat2.a4: It's recommended to arrive 10 minutes early, wear comfortable clothing, bring a blanket, and avoid eating for 2 hours before practice.
cat2.q5: Do I need to reserve my spot?
cat2.a5: Yes, it's recommended to confirm your reservation via WhatsApp before attending.
cat2.a6: Yes, each class shows its level (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced or All Levels) so you can pick the one that suits you.
cat2.a7: Each class shows its price (or "Free" if applicable) and, when applicable, a special price for ACIKY members.

cat3.title: Online Sadhanas (daily virtual practice)
cat3.a1: It's a daily spiritual practice held during the Ambrosial Hours — or Amrit Vela, "the nectar time" — the periods from 4:00 to 7:00 AM and 4:00 to 7:00 PM, when energy is calmest and most receptive. ACIKY offers it virtually to connect the community regardless of location.
cat3.a2: 7:30 to 9:00 AM (Havana time), because the session is guided by a certified teacher joining from Mexico.
cat3.q3: On which platform are sadhanas held?
cat3.q4: How do I join the Online Sadhanas?
cat3.a4: You need to contact ACIKY (via WhatsApp) to receive the access link for the daily sessions.
cat3.q5: What do I need to participate?
cat3.a5: A device with a stable internet connection, clear audio (headphones or speakers), and keeping your microphone muted during the session to preserve the collective atmosphere.
cat3.q6: What is the structure of a sadhana?
cat3.a6: It follows the traditional sequence: a selected pauree (recited 11 times), opening, healing prayer, warm-up, kriya, meditation, and closing prayer.
cat3.q7: Is there a recommended minimum commitment?
cat3.a7: Yes, it's suggested to commit initially to 40 consecutive days to build the habit and experience the full benefits of the practice.
cat3.q8: Can I start little by little?
cat3.a8: Yes, newcomers are encouraged to first join Sunday sessions and gradually add more days over time.
cat3.q9: What preparation is recommended before a sadhana?
cat3.a9: Lay out your clothes and prepare your space the night before, place your alarm clock away from your bed, and drink a glass of water upon waking.
cat3.q10: What benefits does regular sadhana practice bring?
cat3.a10: Greater mental clarity, elevated energy, spiritual connection, inner discipline, emotional stability and sacred community.

cat4.title: Golden Routes (national expansion)
cat4.a1: It's ACIKY's expansion project that brings Kundalini Yoga to communities across all of Cuba's provinces, through certified instructors who travel to teach and drive local practice groups.
cat4.a2: It consists of six stages: identifying the need, planning the route, travel and immersion, intensive teaching, establishing a local group, and ongoing follow-up.
cat4.q3: How can I take part in the Golden Routes?
cat4.a3: There are four ways to get involved: as a traveling instructor (KRI certification, at least 1 year of experience and availability to travel), local host (offering space, coordinating participants or supporting with lodging), emerging leader (receiving free training to sustain the practice in their community), or sponsor (financially supporting transportation, materials or equipment).
cat4.q4: What is the goal of the Golden Routes?
cat4.a4: The vision unfolds progressively: continue covering the 15 provinces (2026 Goal), complete coverage (2027 Goal), and build a self-sustaining network with local instructors in every province (2028 Goal).

cat5.title: Rebirthing Ceremonies
cat5.a1: It's a transformative experience that symbolizes the "death" of the limited ego and the birth of an expanded consciousness, using breathwork (pranayama), mantras, meditation and a symbolic release process ("transforming fire").
cat5.q2: How does the ceremony process work?
cat5.a2: It follows five steps: sacred preparation, transformative breathing, mantras of liberation, the "transformative fire", and final rebirth and integration.
cat5.q3: Who is this experience designed for?
cat5.a3: For people going through life transitions, those seeking to heal emotional or family patterns, those seeking clearer purpose, and generally any spiritual seeker committed to their growth.
cat5.q4: How do I find out about upcoming dates?
cat5.a4: Upcoming ceremonies are announced in the corresponding section of the site; availability can also be checked directly via WhatsApp.

cat6.title: Faro de Luz Festival
cat6.q1: What is the Faro de Luz Festival?
cat6.a1: It's ACIKY's most important annual yoga and wellness event: 3 days of full immersion with teachings, intensive practices, sacred music and the collective energy of the community.
cat6.a2: Traditionally in October, though the exact dates, venue and theme for each edition are confirmed on the festival page, since this information is updated every year.
cat6.a3: All Kundalini Yoga sessions, specialized workshops, sacred music, group meditations, organic vegetarian meals, shared-room accommodation, and access to the private post-festival community.
cat6.q4: Is there any benefit to registering early?
cat6.a4: Check the festival page to see whether the current edition offers early-registration benefits, since these vary from year to year.

cat7.title: Membership for instructors
cat7.q1: Who can become an ACIKY member?
cat7.a1: ACIKY accepts as members Kundalini Yoga instructors with KRI (Kundalini Research Institute) certification at level 1 or higher, the only essential requirement.
cat7.q2: How do I join as a certified instructor?
cat7.a2: Write to ACIKY via WhatsApp or email to start the membership process. You can also check the membership guide available on the site.
cat7.q3: What does participating as a member involve?
cat7.a3: It's not mandatory, but it's highly valued. Members contribute by organizing activities, leading classes, serving the community, attending events, promoting the practice, and exchanging ideas within the collective.
cat7.q4: Is anything asked of members in return?
cat7.a4: For now, the only thing asked is to offer a special price for fellow ACIKY members in their own classes and events.
cat7.q5: Does ACIKY charge a membership fee?
cat7.a5: Contributions to ACIKY are voluntary; each person contributes according to their own conscience and desire to sustain the mission.
cat7.q6: What if I don't have KRI certification yet but want to teach someday?
cat7.a6: ACIKY guides those who feel called to train as instructors on the path to KRI certification; it's recommended to contact us directly for more information.
cat7.q7: Does ACIKY have an evaluation or professional development team?
cat7.a7: Yes, it has a CEU Evaluation Team focused on training and teaching, service (seva) and leadership, research, and additional benefits for instructors. This team also reviews and validates events, workshops and blog articles.

cat8.title: Donations and financial support
cat8.q1: How can I support ACIKY financially?
cat8.a1: Through the site's donations section, via PayPal or bank transfer/Transfermóvil in CUP.
cat8.q2: Why donate to a personal PayPal account instead of an ACIKY account?
cat8.a2: Due to the financial restrictions ACIKY faces as a Cuban organization, a collaborating teacher offers the use of their personal account to receive international donations (the note must state exactly "Donación ACIKY"). Every cent goes entirely to the community.
cat8.q3: What is my donation used for?
cat8.a3: Instructor training, the Faro de Luz Festival, the Golden Routes, regular classes and programs, the Langar (sacred meal), and special ceremonies and events.
cat8.q4: How long does it take to confirm my donation?
cat8.a4: ACIKY verifies payments manually against its PayPal history; confirmation can take up to 48 hours.
cat8.a5: No. They go to ACIKY's general fund; they are not tax-deductible nor refundable once confirmed.

cat9.title: Practice spaces
cat9.a1: These are places, besides ACIKY's core classes, where you can practice Kundalini Yoga in Cuba, each with its own instructor, address, municipality and disciplines.
cat9.q2: Can I filter spaces by municipality?
cat9.a2: Yes, the spaces page allows filtering by municipality.

cat10.title: Blog, testimonials, postures and videos
cat10.q1: Who can publish on ACIKY's blog?
cat10.a1: Only instructors and authorized administrators; the ACIKY CEU Tribunal reviews and validates each article before publishing it.
cat10.q2: Can I leave my testimonial on the site?
cat10.a2: Yes, once logged in you can write your experience from the Testimonials page. Each testimonial is reviewed before publication.
cat10.q3: Where can I find postures and tutorial videos?
cat10.a3: In the "Postures" and "Videos" sections of the site, both with a search feature by name.

cat11.title: Account, privacy and data
cat11.q1: What data does ACIKY collect when I register?
cat11.a1: First name, last name and spiritual name, email address, an optional profile photo, any testimonials you choose to publish, and a functional session cookie.
cat11.q2: Does ACIKY use tracking or advertising cookies?
cat11.a2: No. Only a functional session cookie is used, necessary for logging in.
cat11.q3: Can I delete my account and my data?
cat11.a3: Yes, at any time, by contacting ACIKY via WhatsApp or the contact page.
cat11.q4: What's the minimum age required to create an account?
cat11.q5: I forgot my password, what do I do?
cat11.a5: Use the "Forgot your password?" link on the login screen to receive a password reset email.
cat11.q6: Do I need to create an account to participate?
cat11.a6: The site allows you to sign in or register to access a personal profile, though booking your free first class or joining sadhanas only requires writing via WhatsApp.

cat12.title: Contact
cat12.a1: Via WhatsApp, email (info.aciky@gmail.com), the site's contact form, or through social media (Facebook and Instagram @acikycuba).
cat12.a2: Yes: Facebook, Instagram (@acikycuba) and WhatsApp, all linked in the site's footer.
